stories.head: Iterable CMO on AI-Powered Personalization, Real-Time Decisioning, and Customer Trust
stories.plain: Iterable's CMO Priya Gill explains how brands are moving from batch-and-blast to real-time AI decisioning in customer engagement. She covers personalization at scale, how trust is maintained when AI drives messaging, and what it takes to build continuously improving engagement programs — a practical blueprint for anyone buying or building a CEP.

stories.head: Capacity Adds Multi-Agent Support, Automated QA, and Knowledge Orchestration to Voice AI
stories.plain: Capacity's voice AI now routes complex customer calls across multiple specialist agents that share a single knowledge layer — the same one powering chat. Automated quality assurance scores every call without a human reviewer. This signals how agentic, cross-channel CX platforms are replacing siloed voice bots, raising the bar for what a CEP must do.

stories.head: Liferay Data Platform GA: B2B Unified Account Intelligence Built Into DXP
stories.plain: Liferay has shipped its Data Platform as generally available, giving B2B organizations a unified account-activity layer native to their digital experience platform. Rather than bolting on a separate CDP, teams get account intelligence inside the same system that runs their web experience — a model that could reshape how B2B buyers evaluate CDPs versus DXP-native data stores.

stories.head: Luma's Prince Boucher: Building Generative AI as a Core Capability, Not a Pilot
stories.plain: Boucher argues that the real enterprise risk is not moving too fast with AI but staying in pilot mode indefinitely. He outlines what it takes to shift teams from experimenting with generative AI tools to embedding them into how work is measured and governed — directly relevant to anyone deciding how to scale a MarTech-AI program.

stories.head: Suplari Launches AI Agent That Owns Full Procurement Data Lifecycle and Self-Heals Connectors
stories.plain: Suplari's Data Assistant ingests procurement data in any format, fixes data-quality faults autonomously, and repairs broken connectors when source systems change — without escalating to a human. This is a concrete example of agentic AI taking ownership of a data pipeline, with governance implications for any org considering agents that write back to production systems.

stories.head: Iterable CMO explains AI-powered personalization and real-time decisioning strategy
stories.plain: Iterable's CMO walks through how brands are using AI to move from segment-level messaging to real-time 1:1 decisioning, covering trust guardrails, always-on optimization, and what it takes to build continuously improving engagement programs. Useful for anyone evaluating CEPs or trying to understand what AI-driven personalization looks like in practice today.

stories.head: Liferay Data Platform goes GA, giving B2B teams a DXP-native account intelligence layer
stories.plain: Liferay's new Data Platform is now generally available, providing B2B organisations a unified account-activity view built natively into its digital experience platform. This matters because it shifts CDP-style unification inside the experience layer rather than requiring a separate tool, changing the build-vs-buy calculus for B2B MarTech stacks.

stories.head: Seismic closes Highspot merger; Pipedrive ships MCP connector to Claude
stories.plain: Two structurally significant moves in one news digest: Seismic absorbing Highspot consolidates the sales-enablement market into one dominant player, and Pipedrive's Model Context Protocol link to Claude shows CRMs embedding agentic AI directly into workflows. Both reshape vendor choices for marketing and sales ops teams.

stories.head: Attentive AI Grow lifts email and SMS sign-ups 25%; Calendly ships AI assistant Callie
stories.plain: Attentive's AI growth tool is posting a 25% subscriber list lift across email and SMS channels, while Calendly's new agent Callie handles scheduling autonomously. Both are concrete, measurable deployments — the kind of agentic AI producing verifiable ROI numbers that influence buying decisions at marketing ops level.

stories.head: Space raises $2.4M to build an AI-native filesystem for humans and agents sharing live data
stories.plain: A16z-backed Space is building a distributed filesystem letting both people and AI agents instantly read and write across petabytes of live data with no local storage. For MarTech, this is early infrastructure for multi-agent pipelines — solving the data-access bottleneck that currently limits how fast agentic marketing systems can act.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Move from Pilot to Infrastructure
body: Across the feed, vendors are shipping multi-agent orchestration, knowledge routing, and automated QA as standard product tiers rather than preview features. Capacity's voice platform, Tricentis's agentic dev suite, and Suplari's procurement agent all frame AI as an always-on operational layer, not an experiment.

The strategic shift is that companies are now making build-vs-buy decisions at the infrastructure level — choosing which agent runtime becomes their operating system for work, rather than which AI feature to bolt onto an existing tool. Luma's Prince Boucher articulates this directly: the goal is core capability, not one-off pilots.
ev: Agile Brand · Luma AI as core capability
MarTech Series · Tricentis agentic enterprise dev

themes.head: Intent Data Wired Directly into Sales Execution
body: The Intentsify–Clay partnership is a signal of a broader pattern: intent signals are escaping the analytics dashboard and being injected in real time into the tools reps and campaigns already use. This collapses the lag between a buyer showing interest and a seller acting on it.

For decision-makers this means re-evaluating the architecture of their GTM stack — the value is no longer in which data provider has the best signals, but in which provider can embed those signals closest to the moment of action. Data that lives in a report is worth far less than data that triggers a workflow.
ev: Agile Brand · Liferay Data Platform GA

themes.head: The Value-Proof Gap in CX Investment
body: CustomerGauge's research names a paradox that shows up repeatedly in this period's coverage: operational CX capability is advancing faster than the ability to prove its revenue impact. Teams are deploying more sophisticated tools while still struggling to connect experience improvements to dollar outcomes for the CFO.

The Ai4 expert session reinforces this: selling an AI vision is no longer the hard part — proving tangible value is. Marketers who can close this loop with clear monetization metrics will unlock sustained budget; those who cannot will face consolidation pressure regardless of how advanced their stack is.
ev: Agile Brand · CustomerGauge CX monetization paradox
Agile Brand · Ai4 proving tangible value

themes.head: Brand as an Offensive Asset in an AI World
body: Georgia-Pacific's Jason Ippen reframes brand stewardship not as reputation defence but as a proactive growth lever — particularly important when AI-generated content risks homogenising category messaging. Brave's 51% ROI lift for Regus further shows that premium, brand-safe inventory still delivers measurable advantage over commoditised placements.

The practical implication is a budget reallocation question: as AI lowers the cost of content production, the differentiation value of strong brand identity and curated distribution rises. Marketers need to be intentional about where brand investment goes rather than letting automation fill the space by default.

themes.head: AI-Native Research & Content Workflows Emerge
body: BioBrain's AI-native research OS and Medeo AI's real-time trend discovery for video creation represent a generation of tools built AI-first rather than AI-augmented. They don't add AI to an existing research or production process; they redesign the workflow around continuous, machine-speed data ingestion and synthesis.

For marketing leaders this compresses the insight-to-execution cycle from weeks to hours. The competitive risk is asymmetric: teams still relying on periodic research reports and manual content briefing will be structurally slower than rivals who have wired live intelligence into their creative and campaign pipelines.

month.takeaway: The month's news resolves into a single pressure: AI is shifting from a feature layer to the operating system of go-to-market, research, and brand work — and the companies that treat it as infrastructure rather than a pilot will set the pace everyone else has to match.
